verdict: Apple's sales fell 4% to $90.8B as iPhone revenue dropped 10%, but Services set another all-time record at $23.9B and EPS hit a March-quarter record — it kept $23.6B as profit.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: a March-quarter record; vs $1.52 a year ago

segments.name: iPhone
segments.note: Apple's flagship phone — sales fell 10% from a strong year-ago quarter.

segments.name: Mac
segments.note: Mac computers — up 4%, helped by the MacBook Air with the M3 chip, launched in March.

segments.name: iPad
segments.note: Tablets — down 17% with no new models in the quarter; the redesigned iPad Pro and iPad Air arrived in May, just after the quarter ended.

segments.name: Wearables, Home and Accessories
segments.note: Apple Watch, AirPods and home devices — down 10%; Apple Vision Pro, the $3,499 headset, launched in February but was still a tiny part of sales.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, TV+ and advertising — an all-time record, up 14%.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing future iPhones, Macs, chips and services.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Stores, marketing and running the company day to day.

follow100Note: Services alone is $26.30 of every $100 Apple takes in. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Segments are net sales by product category, as Apple reports them.

takeaways.title: Services set another record
takeaways.text: Services revenue reached $23.9B, an all-time high, up 14% — more than a quarter of everything Apple sells now comes from subscriptions, the App Store and other services.

takeaways.title: iPhone had a soft quarter
takeaways.text: iPhone revenue fell 10% to $46.0B and Greater China sales fell 8% to $16.4B, while Mac grew 4% on the new M3 MacBook Air.

takeaways.title: A bigger buyback
takeaways.text: Apple authorized another $110B of share repurchases and raised its dividend 4% to $0.25 a share — its twelfth straight annual increase.
